nodes.label: AI insurance-document verification and fraud scoring
PDF text extraction preferred; GPT-4o vision only when the PDF yields under 50 chars
Confidence bands: auto-approve at 0.85, auto-reject under 0.60, human review between
Five-check fraud risk score: expiry, date inversion, doc validity, missing identity, tamper keywords
Weighted field-completeness score, then halved in proportion to fraud risk
Every extraction failure still returns success and flags manual review instead of blocking the customer
Rationale: 'pending' is written instead of 'needs_review' because that is not a valid ai_scan_status value
Rationale: Deno's base64 encoder avoids the stack overflow that spread-encoding a large file causes
Rationale: fraud_risk_score and verification_decision live inside ai_extracted_data because the columns may not exist
Primary then fallback OpenAI key retry, with is_fallback stamped into the usage ledger
Deferred refund scheduling against a captured payment
Only a payment already in capture_status 'captured' may be scheduled for refund
Scheduling only writes a reminder_events row; a separate processor performs the actual Stripe refund
A failed reminder_events insert is only warned about, so the payment can be marked scheduled with nothing to execute it
Rationale: errors return HTTP 200 with success:false to avoid a generic FunctionsHttpError in the Supabase JS client
Additional-driver licence-verification invite using the in-house AI flow, not Veriff
Additional drivers are not customers: identity_verifications.customer_id is NULL and routing rides on external_user_id
Three-hour QR session TTL matching create-ai-verification-session, with operator resend as the recovery path
Driver row stamped with verification_url and identity_verification_id so the rental page can show Resend / Open
Rationale: the verification row is the durable artefact, so a Resend or driver-row-update failure is non-fatal
Rationale: 200 with success:false so the client reads data.error instead of a generic non-2xx throw
Caller's app_users.tenant_id must match the driver's tenant, with a super-admin bypass
Auto-extension pay-link reminders, manual operator send and cron nudge sweep
One function, two entry modes: a rentalId body is an operator action, an empty body is the cron sweep
Operator-chosen weekday evaluated in the tenant's timezone supersedes the N-day interval cadence
An existing live checkout_url is reused; only a custom amount forces a fresh Stripe session
Pending payments row pre-created against the checkout session so the Stripe webhook can settle it
Rationale: CORS headers and the Resend sender are vendored inline to keep the function single-file deployable
New charges route to the tenant's current platform account: managed uses UK keys, own uses UAE keys
Every send lands in auto_extension_reminders so the control panel can show history, calendar and recipient
Reminder-created payments carry booking_source 'auto_extend' and Extension target_categories
The outstanding week is resolved from the rental_extension_totals view, not recomputed locally
Bonzah go-live confirmation email to the operator
Caller must carry app_users.is_bonzah_partner or is_super_admin
Recipient precedence: the submission's primary contact email, then the tenant admin email
The reviewer's partner_message is surfaced verbatim inside the activation email
Bonzah 'needs a small update' email sent when an application is rejected
Rationale: a rejection is deliberately framed as friendly next steps, never as blame or refusal
submission.reject_reason is rendered to the operator as the 'What to update' block
Full Bonzah application forwarded to the Bonzah underwriting contact
brandon_sent_at upserted on tenant_onboarding_checklist as the send receipt the onboarding UI reads
The recipient address is operational config in admin_settings.bonzah_brandon_email, not code
Bank routing/account numbers and full card PAN, expiry and CVC are rendered into the outbound email body
Super admins may send any tenant's form; a tenant's own staff may send theirs, which powers the auto-fire on submit
Only the most recent submission per tenant is ever sent
Legacy booking-confirmation email with branding resolved and templated inline
Tenant branding is re-queried and re-templated here rather than reusing the shared Resend branding service
Posts straight to the Resend API with a global FROM_EMAIL, bypassing tenant-slug sender resolution
Booking-confirmed email to the customer plus a preference-gated operator new-booking email
Operator copy gated on the 'bookings' email preference and routed to the tenant notification recipient; the customer copy is never gated
Rationale: the plate is blanked at source because it appears in the subject line and leaks without the mail being opened
Rationale: in-app notifications are created by the frontend, so this function is email-only to avoid duplicates
Vehicle-collection and lockbox WhatsApp message with photo attachments
Rationale: PostgREST returns errors rather than throwing, so the old try/catch never fired and the privacy check failed OPEN
Rationale: the plate is blanked before templating because a custom template substitutes vehicle_reg directly and no per-message guard would reach it
A tenant's WhatsApp lockbox template wins, else the SMS template body is reused
Body truncated at WhatsApp's 4096-char limit; at most 10 photos, each a separate best-effort image message
Doubles as the platform's generic Meta WhatsApp sender for callers with no collection semantics
Marketing-site contact-form relay into the operator inbox
Submitter-controlled name, subject and message are interpolated into the email HTML without escaping
The 'Received' timestamp is rendered in a hardcoded America/New_York timezone regardless of tenant
Close-protection (executive security) enquiry relay — a non-rental vertical inside the platform
Drive 917 branding, UK phone and London address are hardcoded; no tenant lookup and no Supabase client at all
Risk level drives both the subject line and colour-coded triage in the operator email
Staff-to-customer email sent from the realtime chat inbox and mirrored into the chat thread
The outbound email is recorded as a chat_channel_messages row with channel 'email' and the Resend id as external_id
chat_channels.last_message_at and last_channel are updated so the inbox sorts and labels correctly
If the message insert fails after Resend accepted the mail, the caller sees an error although the customer received it
Super admins may supply tenantId in the body; tenant staff are pinned to their own app_users.tenant_id
Excess-mileage charge: Stripe pay-link plus a branded customer email
Pending 'Excess Mileage' payments row keyed by stripe_checkout_session_id for webhook settlement
Rationale: the plate must be redacted where the Stripe product description is BUILT, because Stripe renders it on Checkout and in the receipt, which cannot be retracted
A failed payments insert only logs, leaving a payable Stripe link with no local row for the webhook to settle
Installment charge-failure notice to the customer plus a gated operator alert
Rationale: the old redaction blanked data.vehicle.reg, an object the email never read, so the plate shipped in 100% of these emails
record_installment_notification RPC logs a 'payment_failed' entry against the installment
Customer copy promises an automatic retry rather than asking for immediate payment, matching the charge cron's behaviour
Installment payment receipt carrying plan progress
Receipt renders paid/total installments, total paid, remaining and a progress bar from installment_plans aggregates
Rationale: identical wrong-object plate bug to send-installment-failed; redact at composition, not on the request payload
record_installment_notification RPC logs a 'payment_success' entry against the installment
Overdue installment reminders: cron sweep of active plans plus direct invoke after a failed charge
One link settles every overdue installment at once; the latest overdue slot is stamped as installmentId so the webhook can call installment_settle_invoice
Cron mode honours a 24-hour cadence anchored on installment_plans.last_reminder_sent_at
Documentation drift: the header still describes a /pay/<token> magic link, but the code now embeds the Stripe Checkout URL directly and genToken is dead
Rationale: success and cancel origins must never send a customer to localhost even if an admin tested locally
A failed checkout creation still writes an installment_notifications row with status 'failed' before bailing out
Invoice and payment-link email accepting three different input shapes
invoiceId, rentalId, or a bare payment URL plus amount all synthesise the same invoice-like object
Rationale: hidePlate was read as a free variable from another function's scope — a ReferenceError that made EVERY invoice and payment-link email throw before sending
Deposit-hold notice tells the customer a separate authorisation follows the charge on the same card
Rationale: setup_future_usage off_session saves the card so create-deposit-hold can preauth the deposit on the same payment method
Pending payments row pre-created against the session so the Stripe webhook can find and update it
A Stripe failure degrades to an invoice email with no Pay Now button rather than failing the send
The account-level branch carries the collect-then-decide credit flow: money with no invoice and no rental
Multi-channel outbound sender for a lead conversation: sms, email, whatsapp or internal note
Message row inserted as 'queued', dispatched, then updated to sent or failed with the provider message id
Every send writes a lead_activity event and touches conversations plus leads last_message_at
Rationale: the {{variable}} substitution pattern is re-implemented here rather than shared with the lockbox and template renderers
Rationale: WhatsApp piggybacks on send-collection-whatsapp as a generic Meta send until a dedicated wrapper exists
channel 'note' is internal-only: direction 'internal', status 'sent', no provider dispatch
Dispatch failures return 200 with status 'failed' so the inbox can render a failed bubble instead of erroring
systemTriggered flips sender_type and actor_type to 'system', which is how automations attribute their sends
Cron that releases lockbox codes once the tenant's post-approval delay has elapsed
Send time equals rentals.approved_at plus tenants.lockbox_send_offset_minutes
rentals.lockbox_sent_at being NULL is the only guard against re-sending a code
tenants.lockbox_notification_methods decides the email / sms / whatsapp flags passed to notify-lockbox-code
Every attempt lands in lockbox_send_log with sent/failed, the channel list and the scheduled time
A vehicle with no lockbox_code is skipped with only a console warning and no lockbox_send_log row
Cross-cutting pattern: any pay-link sender pre-inserts a Pending payments row keyed by stripe_checkout_session_id so the webhook settles rather than creates
Cross-cutting pattern: every outbound notification sender resolves hide_vehicle_registration once and redacts where the vehicle string is composed

hyperedges.label: Plate-privacy redaction repeated across six independent notification senders
Pay-link send to webhook settlement: pre-created Pending payment keyed by checkout session
Scheduled lockbox key handover: approval delay, channel preferences, delivery and audit log
